title: Baguette Tennis Necklace
ingredient: an ivory raw-silk potli with a gold zari border and gold tassels, the necklace spilling from its mouth
rhyme: the potli every wedding guest carries = where this necklace travels; ivory, gold and blush, the shaadi palette
notes: r02a: one row of crosswise baguettes in gold box settings, four corner claws and a window on each box side, as in the listing; both ends stay inside the potli, so the clasp is hidden. The stones read a little large beside a 15 cm potli (the model draws fine lines slightly big). Calm blush plaster top left for the words.
replaces: Agra petha: translucent sugar-crusted rectangles on an old brass plate

title: Prism Rivière Bracelet
ingredient: sugared almonds in aqua, pink and butter yellow, in an old silver katori
rhyme: the three pastel stones = the three pastel dragées of an Indian wedding favour
notes: Cushion stones in double pave halos with bead claws and gallery windows, fold-over clasp; no two neighbours share a colour. Variant b turned the plaster into travertine and crowded the frame.

title: Woven Gold Hoops
ingredient: the woven gold zari paisley border of an ivory Banarasi silk saree
rhyme: braided gold hoops beside woven gold zari: Banarasi weaving, made to wear
notes: r04a: a thick braid of many fine gold strands, the flat polished disc inside the top and the hinged latch wire, both hoops round and identical, as in the listing. The zari border is about two and a half hoops wide. The top tenth is soft out-of-focus fold; calm ivory silk top left for the words.
replaces: three ripe golden wheat ears, loose grains and a bristle

title: Verdant Eternity Band
ingredient: an open emerald-green velvet ring box with an ivory satin lid
rhyme: a ring belongs in a ring box: the moment before yes, in the green of its stones
notes: r05a: oval green stones in four claws, the fine clear pave wave scalloping round each oval, cool silver tone, as in the listing; the open back sits down in the slot. True scale: the ring is about a third of the 5 cm box. Plain lining, no text. Calm mint plaster top left for the words.
replaces: freshly shelled hara chana in an old brass katori, a papery pod

title: Baguette Tennis Bracelet
ingredient: a blank ivory wedding invitation with a gold-foil border, an embossed gold paisley and a sprig of baby's breath
rhyme: the wedding invitation, and the bracelet you will wear to it
notes: r07a: crosswise baguettes in gold box settings with four corner claws and a box clasp with its safety catch, fastened in a round, as in the listing; the line is a true 6 mm beside a 13 cm card. The card carries no writing. Calm dove-grey plaster top left for the words.
replaces: a soft mound of raw long-grain basmati rice with a trail of single grains spilling into the bracelet

title: Silk Mesh Cuff
ingredient: two lacy discs of pheni (hair-fine fried vermicelli nests), a broken piece, loose threads
rhyme: the fine woven gold mesh = the hair-fine golden threads of pheni
notes: Mesh exact (fine milanese weave rolled into a tube), polished oval end caps facing across the gap. Pheni reads real with a caramelised centre. Cuff to pheni 1.29, true 1.25. 13a enlarged the cuff and cut the pheni at the frame edge. Spelled pheni, not feni (the Goan spirit).

title: Marquise Layering Set
ingredient: a cut stem of rajnigandha (tuberose) with long closed creamy buds, three fallen buds
rhyme: clear pointed marquise stones = the pointed creamy tuberose buds; rajnigandha, the night-fragrant flower
notes: Set exact: two separate fine cable chains; short one with one 13mm marquise; lariat with the Y pear, two marquise stations spaced apart and a pear tip, five stones in all. Big marquise about half a bud, true scale. 14b lost a marquise station on the lariat drop.

title: Ribbon Bead Bracelet
ingredient: a handmade ivory card mithai box tied with one fine gold zari thread in a bow
rhyme: the hair-fine gold chain = the gold zari thread; the two-heart stone bow = the thread bow; Diwali gifting
notes: Bow exact: two clear hearts meeting at a gold centre bar in fine claws; satellite beads and lobster clasp true. Hearts about 5.7mm against 5mm true. The only non-ingredient prop of the set, chosen for Diwali gifting. 15a had harder light and hearts about 6.3mm.

title: Lilac Papillon Ring
ingredient: a drift of fallen lavender jacaranda blossoms, two loose petals
rhyme: the pale lilac pave wings = the lavender of jacaranda; a butterfly landed among fallen flowers
notes: Ring exact: lilac micro-pave wings in raised gold rims, polished body bar, open clear-stone outline offset behind, slim shank. Butterfly about two thirds of a blossom, near true. 18a enlarged the ring about 1.5x and set it on a plinth edge.

title: Aqua Heart Drops
ingredient: a small hand-painted Jaipur blue-pottery dish in white, pale aqua and soft blue, one chip on the rim
rhyme: the pale icy aqua heart = the pale turquoise glaze of Jaipur blue pottery; Jaipur is the Pink City
notes: 19a/19b lying flat drifted: small pave and baguettes on the front and earrings about 1.7x the dish. Reshot standing face-on as in the listing front view: 19c shows the six large round stones in claws down each C and the pale aqua heart on its loop. The dish has no fixed size, so scale reads plausible. Second non-ingredient prop (a Jaipur craft).

title: Prism Cluster Studs
ingredient: three cones of Diwali rangoli powder (violet, baby pink, marigold yellow) and a fingertip drawing the first curved stroke
rhyme: violet, pink and yellow stones = the three rangoli colours; the smiling arc = the first rangoli stroke
notes: Studs exact and mirrored: purple princess, pink baguette, large yellow emerald cut, purple princess, pink baguette, tiny pearls in the gaps. The model added a fingertip drawing the stroke despite the no-hands line; kept, as it is natural, soft-focus and gives true scale (studs about 1.4x). 20a sat on a plinth edge with scattered specks.

title: Baguette Halo Drops
ingredient: two white shevanti (chrysanthemum) flower heads and loose petals, the Diwali-season flower
rhyme: the sunburst of slim clear baguettes = the narrow white rays of a chrysanthemum; pearls = its white
notes: Earrings exact: flat gold disc, about 30 radiating baguettes, beaded ring, 5mm pearl centre, 10mm round pearl drop on a loop. Disc about 1.3x true against the 5cm flower. 23a drew the discs about 1.5x and the flowers sharp.

title: Verdant Cushion Studs
ingredient: two fresh paan (betel) leaves and one whole clove, the pin of a folded paan
rhyme: deep emerald cushion stones = the glossy deep green of a paan leaf; the clove is the paan pin and the scale proof
notes: 24a/24b drew the studs about 30mm against the leaf (2.3x). Reshot with a clove (15mm) beside them and a critical-scale block: 24c studs about one clove long, true. Studs exact: emerald cushion in a polished silver bezel inside a single scalloped halo of clear rounds. Line plays on the song Khaike paan Banaras wala.

title: Quatrefoil Éclat Studs
ingredient: freshly fallen parijat (harsingar, night jasmine) flowers, white petals on saffron-orange tubes
rhyme: clear pear stones radiating from a gold centre = white parijat petals around a saffron-gold tube; the studs lie like two more fallen flowers
notes: Studs exact: sharp four-point star with inward curves, single pave outline, four outward pear stones in gold frames, round centre in a four-lobed flower, open gaps. Each stud about one flower, true. 25a added leaves and a branch.

title: Baguette Eternity Band
ingredient: a loose pinch of Kashmiri saffron (kesar) threads, two loose threads and a faint saffron stain
rhyme: the raspberry-ruby baguettes = the crimson of kesar threads; saffron is worth more than gold by weight
notes: 28a/28b copied the listing hero edge-on, so the band read as a bar. Reshot lying on its side at 35 degrees: 28c reads as a ring of crosswise ruby baguettes in corner claws. Against mongra threads of 1.5-2cm the ring is within about 1.3x. Ruby stock is low (7 of 25; Emerald 9, Amethyst 9).

title: Heartbead Bracelet
ingredient: edible silver dragees, a soft heap with a few rolled loose towards the bracelet
rhyme: the mirror-silver steel beads = bigger twins of the silver dragees on mithai and cakes; the gold heart is the one warm note
notes: 29b: beads grey-gunmetal mirror steel as every listing photo reads them, gold T-bar, round toggle and one puffed heart on its jump ring, small end beads at the clasp. Bead-to-heart ratio about 0.5, the same as the cube listing close-up. Dragees about half a bead, bright and soft-focus behind. 29a drew the dragees as spare 6mm beads in the same grey, so the rhyme collapsed into loose beads.

title: Duo Link Bracelet
ingredient: a block of golden gur with broken crumbs beside a heap of white sugar (cheeni)
rhyme: gold links and silver links = gur and cheeni, the two sweeteners every Indian kitchen asks you to choose between
notes: 41a matches the listing hero link for link: three silver and five gold long ovals, stacked gold-ring connectors, two places where gold links hook straight into each other as in the listing, lobster clasp and extender. Link about half the 4cm gur block. Asked for stone-grey plaster and got warm cream, which suits the gur. 41b had the grey ground but a different link order with a silver-to-gold direct hook.

title: Mint Pear Drop Earrings
ingredient: a green nashpati, one whole and one cut half, with one loose seed on the plaster
rhyme: the pale mint pear-cut stone = the pale green pear; the loose seed is the stone in brown
notes: 42a/42b drew the earrings about 1.6x against the pear (about a third of its height). Reshot touching the cut half with a loose pear seed as the referent: 42c has three clear pears stepping to the mint pear in claws on each earring, the mint stone about 1.3x the seed (true about 1x) and the earring about a quarter of the pear. 42d drew them about 1.4x.

title: Marquise Coil Cuff
ingredient: magaz (peeled melon seeds), a loose heap with a pair of seeds beside the cuff
rhyme: each marquise stone is the size and shape of a melon seed, and the two slanted rows read like seeds sown in a herringbone
notes: 45a: two rows of marquise stones in gold claw cups slanting in opposite directions as in the listing, plain polished back band with a ball at each end. Seeds about 1.3x a stone against about 1.2x true; cuff about 1.1x. 45b equally faithful with a calmer top left but slightly milky stones.

title: Toggle Link Chain
ingredient: brass paper clips, one clipped to a sheet of deckled ivory cotton paper
rhyme: open paperclip links = brass paper clips, gold on gold; the office clip, promoted to jewellery
notes: 51a: open elongated paperclip links, the heavy spring-gate ring with its push-pin nub and a short pavé bar of about 8 stones lying across it, as in the listing. Ring about half a paper clip and each link about a third, true for 15 mm, 11 mm and 33 mm clips. Clips on the paper at the upper right, calm plaster top left. 51b was as faithful but piled the clips in the calm corner.

title: Baguette Tennis Necklace
ingredient: a small cut-crystal perfume bottle with a gold collar, golden perfume
rhyme: perfume and the necklace are the last two things you put on before you leave; step-cut glass beside step-cut stones
notes: r52b: crosswise baguettes in gold box settings with corner claws and side windows, as in the listing; the box clasp lies unfastened, the two ends apart, as if about to be put on. Honest scale beside an 8 cm bottle. r52a was as faithful but the low angle showed a window and wall in the top third.
replaces: a fresh mogra gajra, white jasmine buds strung tight on cotton thread

title: Prism Rivière Bracelet
ingredient: three origami paper boats in pastel aqua, pink and butter yellow, with a few raindrops
rhyme: aqua, pink and yellow stones = aqua, pink and yellow paper boats on a little stream; the monsoon game every child played, made precious
notes: 53e: square pastel stones in double pavé halos with corner claws, joined halo to halo in silver tone, in a strict aqua, pink, yellow order; exactly three boats; calm upper half. Reshot twice: 53a had no calm corner for the words, 53b put chain links between the stones and star glints on them, 53c set two pinks side by side, 53d drew a fourth boat and only 12 stones, 53f stood a boat on its tip. The stones read a little bolder than 5 mm beside 3 cm boats; there is no fixed-size referent, so the bracelet still reads true.

title: Woven Gold Hoops
ingredient: a wide, low hand-woven cane jewellery tray
rhyme: where everyday hoops live: a braid of gold strands lying on a weave of cane
notes: r54b: a braid of many fine gold strands, the flat disc inside the top and the hinged latch, both round, as in the listing. The hoops read a little large in the tray (about 1.4x; the model draws them big beside cane); the tray runs off the right edge. r54a leaned one hoop on the rim and drew it about twice its size. Calm plaster top left for the words.
replaces: a golden silk paranda, a three-strand plait ending in a tassel bound with zari

title: Cushion Halo Ring
ingredient: a dandelion seed head, with three seeds drifting free
ground: pale dove-grey lime plaster with a hint of lilac
rhyme: a ring of tiny stones around one bright centre = a sphere of tiny parachutes around one centre; blow, and make a wish
notes: 55a: one round brilliant in four claws inside a single-row cushion halo, pavé down both shoulders, silver tone, as in the listing; the ring stands on its band beside the seed head with three seeds rising to the right. The halo is a little under half the seed head, true for 12 mm and a 30 mm head. 55b was faithful and slightly truer in scale, but a bright window filled the calm top.

title: Verdant Eternity Band
ingredient: a mehendi cone and a freshly piped leafy henna vine on handmade paper
rhyme: the green ovals cradled in a wave of clear stones = a mehendi bel; the vine runs straight into the ring: wedding season, and the green that stays
notes: r56a: oval green stones in four claws, the clear pave wave scalloping round each, the open adjustable back with looped tips, cool silver tone, as in the listing. Real glossy henna paste. The ring reads slightly large beside the piped leaves. Calm ivory paper top left for the words.
replaces: a fresh money plant cutting, three marbled heart-shaped leaves on a short vine

title: Baguette Tennis Bracelet
ingredient: an ivory duchess-satin kiss-lock evening clutch
rhyme: a night out: the clutch and the bracelet go on last; crystal and gold on evening plum
notes: r57a: crosswise baguettes in box settings with corner claws and the box clasp with its fold-over safety, lying unfastened in an S, as in the listing; true fineness beside an 18 cm clutch. The clutch runs off the right edge. A dark frame: the words sit in cream.
replaces: the ivory keys of an old teak harmonium

title: Baguette Huggies
ingredient: a small stack of green glass bangles, kaanch ki choodiyan, with fine gold lines
rhyme: small gold hoops with a row of green stones = the green glass bangles they sit inside; choodiyan for the wrist, choodi for the ears
notes: 58b: both huggies stand inside the top bangle, each with one row of seven crosswise emerald baguettes in gold claws on the front half, plain gold behind and the hinge below, as in the listing. Each huggie is about a quarter of a bangle across, true for 15 mm and 6 cm. The glass throws soft green light onto the plaster. 58a was as faithful with the huggies lying flat and overlapping.

title: Bold Nocturne Chain
ingredient: a handmade school paper chain, loops of gold foil paper glued link through link
rhyme: chunky gold oval links = the gold paper loops of a craft-class chain, curve over curve; the chain you made at seven, grown up
notes: 59a: chunky elongated oval links in polished gold, each threaded through the next, with exactly one fully pavé link of the same size at the front, as in the listing. The paper loops show their grey paper backs and uneven glued joins, so they read as a real handmade chain. Paper and gold arc in parallel with a calm top. 59b was faithful but its foil loops looked like crumpled cuffs rather than paper.

title: Bold Nocturne Bracelet
ingredient: a small lit terracotta diya with ghee and a cotton wick
rhyme: a ring of gold links glowing around the flame = the diya's own glow; the pavé link catches the light like the wick
notes: 60a: chunky elongated oval links in polished gold, one fully pavé link at the front, the lobster clasp and the extender ending in a small flat oval tag, as in the listing; the bracelet circles the diya with room to spare and never touches the flame. The diya looks handmade, with ghee, a twisted cotton wick and a soot mark at the spout. 60b was as faithful, with a larger diya crowding the links.

title: Halo Curve Ring
ingredient: three glass marbles (kanche), two amber cat's-eyes and one champagne swirl
rhyme: a banded tiger's eye and a champagne crystal = an amber cat's-eye marble and a clear one; the kanche game, kept for good
notes: 61b: an open bypass band of thin gold wire ending in a banded tiger's eye cabochon and a faceted champagne crystal, each in its own slim bezel, as in the listing and the earlier passed plates; the ring stands upright behind three marbles that throw amber light onto the plaster. Each stone is about three quarters of a marble, true for 12 mm stones and 16 mm marbles. 61a was as faithful but spread the marbles out, with one cut by the frame edge.

title: Kiss Knot Bangle
ingredient: a small cream envelope of handmade paper, sealed with gold wax pressed with a heart
rhyme: the polished X where the bangle crosses = the X of a kiss, set beside a letter sealed with a heart; gold wax, gold bangle
notes: 62a: a finely ribbed snake-coil bangle in gold tone whose ends cross in one polished X, as in the listing; it rests on the envelope with the X beside the seal. The seal carries only a pressed heart, no letters. The bangle is about two thirds of the envelope's width, true for 6 cm and a small 9 cm envelope. 62b was faithful but cut the bangle at the frame edge.

title: Marquise Layering Set
ingredient: a small paper patang of champagne tissue on a bamboo spine and bow
rhyme: the diamond-shaped marquise = the diamond-shaped patang above it, and the lariat's long fine drop = the kite's string; Uttarayan in miniature
notes: 64b: two separate fine cable chains; the short one carries one large marquise point-down, the Y-lariat meets at a small pear and its drop carries two marquise stations and a pear tip, five stones in all, as in the listing. The kite is a tissue patang on a bamboo spine and bow; the short necklace passes under it and trails out by its tail. Five other frames miscounted the lariat (64a, 64c, 64e, 64f) or ended it in a marquise with a star glint (64d), so 64b stays even though its chains run off the left edge; the Feed carries the words at the bottom left, clear of every chain.

title: Ribbon Bead Bracelet
ingredient: a white satin school ribbon tied in a double-loop bow with V-cut tails
rhyme: two heart stones meeting at a gold bar = the satin bow Mummy tied at the end of every plait; white on navy, like the uniform
notes: 66b: a fine gold cable chain with small satellite beads and, at the centre, two separate heart-cut clear stones in claws meeting at a tiny gold bar, plus the lobster clasp and extender, as in the listing. The crystal bow is about a fifth of the satin bow, a touch large for 10 mm beside a 6 cm bow (the model always draws it slightly big). 66a was faithful but showed a bright wall above the navy. A navy frame: the words sit in cream.

title: Rivière Eternal Bracelet
ingredient: a Diwali ladi of tiny warm fairy-light bulbs on fine copper wire
rhyme: one long row of tiny round stones = one long row of tiny warm bulbs; the Diwali ladi that never fuses
notes: 67a: one continuous row of round brilliant clear stones, each in its own four-prong gold basket and linked stone to stone, with the polished interlocking box clasp sitting in the line like a buckle, as in the listing; the bracelet runs between two loops of a warm fairy-light string. Each stone is a little larger than a 3 mm bulb, true to the 3 to 4 mm the photos show. The bulbs glow as soft round lights, no star glints. 67b was faithful with the clasp at the end of the line.

title: Bold Dome Huggies
ingredient: a string of brass ghungroo bells on a red cotton cord
rhyme: a polished gold dome = a polished brass ghungroo bell, the same round swell and warm shine; one rings, one does not
notes: 68a: two chunky mirror-polished huggies that swell at the bottom and taper to a slim hinged bar, no texture and no stones, as in the listing; one stands and one lies inside the curve of the bell string. Each huggie is about one and a half bells wide, true for 16 mm hoops and 10 mm ghungroo. 68b was as faithful, with darker antique bells.
